correctness.rationale: A.e. differentiability of a convex boundary gives the exact translated radial derivative with no smoothness requirement. A support-ball inclusion uniformly controls all directions; polar volume and the cone-area Jacobian give the log-cosh limit and cancel its odd term via the divergence theorem. Equi-Lipschitz estimates upgrade convergence to uniform on compact sets. Ordinary covariogram overlap and its universal projection-body directional derivative bound all critical sublevels; thus they converge globally in Hausdorff metric. Strict convexity of the limiting integrand and the sharp cubical radii are analytically proved. Independent quadrature on a triangle and square agrees across multiple smoothing parameters. Neither finite tests nor external records replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source proves critical convergence only under C3 boundary regularity. The previous cubical nonsmooth result covers one special class, while an earlier all-convex-body study concerns the integral-defined level bodies rather than convergence of the radial smoothing. The present theorem newly proves locally uniform functional convergence and global Hausdorff convergence for every convex body using almost-everywhere radial first variation and the universal covariogram deficit. No encompassing primary result was found in the inspected literature or mathematical records, but priority remains provisional.

The cube specialization is already known and has no independent originality claim.

value.rationale: The actual critical smoothing limit is generalized from C3 boundaries and a previously analyzed cube to every full-dimensional convex body, filling a natural regularity gap at the new Orlicz transition and supplying a reusable a.e.-boundary method and global localization argument. The sharp cubical Euclidean contact picture is a calibration, not an attempt to promote the previously known cube limit into a separate result.
